definitions.gloss: Shinjuku; the Tokyo district of skyscrapers, shopping, and nightlife
definitions.explanation: A major district in western Tokyo built around Shinjuku Station, the busiest railway station in the world. It combines the high-rise office quarter and city hall on the west side with department stores, bars, and the Kabukicho entertainment area on the east.

examples.japanese: {新宿|しんじゅく}で{乗|の}り{換|か}える。
{新宿|しんじゅく}{駅|えき}は{出口|でぐち}が{多|おお}くて{迷|まよ}いやすい。
examples.english: Shinjuku Station has so many exits that it's easy to get lost.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}のあと{新宿|しんじゅく}で{飲|の}んで、{終電|しゅうでん}ぎりぎりに{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: After work we drank in Shinjuku and got home just in time for the last train.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {新宿|しんじゅく}{駅|えき}: Shinjuku Station
- {西新宿|にししんじゅく}: the skyscraper and city-hall side
- {歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう}: the nightlife quarter east of the station
- {新宿|しんじゅく}{御苑|ぎょえん}: Shinjuku Gyoen, the large garden park

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Because so many lines meet there, {新宿|しんじゅく}{駅|えき} is a byword for crowds and for getting lost — its underground passages are a standing joke. The district also serves in fiction as shorthand for the restless, anonymous side of Tokyo.
